workflows.name: Installer & Contractor Network Strategy, Trade-Coverage & Capacity Design

Automation Opportunity: - Coverage/capacity modeling; trade-area analytics; economics simulator; KPI dashboards
Controls: - CTL-746 (ensure controlled execution — Installer/Contractor Network Strategy, Recruitment & Vetting (PA-172.1).)
- CTL-746: strategy board-approved; coverage targets set; build-vs-partner split defined; KPIs tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-12 (own crews), VS-11/VS-43/VS-107 (B2B/trade/key accounts), VS-95 (marketplace), VS-33 (strategy), VS-37 (expansion), W4991 (coverage), W4997 (economics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Coverage-gap risk**: Insufficient installers in a trade/area → unfulfilled referrals; mitigated by coverage design (W4991)
- **Channel-conflict risk**: Network installers competing with BuildRight's own crews (VS-12); mitigated by the build-vs-partner split
- **Economics risk**: Referral fees too low/high → installer disinterest or customer friction; mitigated by economics modeling (W4997)
System Touchpoints: - Strategy/FP&A (VS-33/VS-17.4); services (VS-12); B2B/trade (VS-11/VS-43); marketplace platform (VS-95); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Set the installer-network strategy & operating model: the referral-vs-managed-marketplace model, the trade specialties covered (electrical, plumbing, carpentry, tiling, paint, HVAC/solar, appliance, roofing, masonry), the own-crew (VS-12) vs network split, the geographic/trade-coverage targets, the referral economics (W4997), and the positioning ("Your Home Building Partner")

Design trade-coverage & capacity: per trade-area (region/province) the required installer count/capacity by specialty, the tier model (preferred/standard), the service-level targets (response, quote, completion), and the build-vs-partner decision per trade

Build the business case & govern: referral-fee/commission economics, attach/CLV impact, the platform/ops cost, KPIs (coverage %, fill-rate, rating, conversion), board/leadership approval, and integration with services (VS-12), trade (VS-43), and store opening (VS-37)

workflows.name: Contractor Vetting, PCAB License (RA 4566) & Insurance Verification

Automation Opportunity: - License/insurance register auto-verify; lapse-monitoring (W5006); onboarding gate; TPRM integration
Controls: - CTL-746: PCAB/insurance verified before onboarding; evidence captured; onboarding gated; re-verification scheduled (W5006)
Cross-references: - links to VS-165 (PCAB/RA 4566), VS-166 (license portfolio), VS-100 (legal), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-26 (insurance), VS-116 (surety), W4988 (DD), W4989 (onboarding), W5006 (re-verification)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unlicensed risk**: Referring an unlicensed contractor (RA 4566) → illegal contract, customer harm, BuildRight liability; mitigated by PCAB verification gate
- **Uninsured risk**: Installer without adequate insurance → uncovered liability; mitigated by insurance verification
- **Lapse risk**: License/insurance lapses after onboarding; mitigated by periodic re-verification (W5006)
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/license (VS-165/VS-22/VS-166); legal (VS-100); TPRM (VS-161); insurance (VS-26); surety (VS-116); marketplace platform (VS-95)

steps.activity: Verify licenses & legal eligibility: PCAB contractor license (RA 4566 — links VS-165, verify it's the *contractor's* license, current, correct category), DTI/SEC registration, BIR registration, mayor's/LGU permit, and trade-specific licenses (electrical license, plumbing, FPA for pesticides, etc.); verify against official registers

Verify insurance & bonding: public-liability/professional indemnity insurance (current, adequate limits, BuildRight named/added insured where required), performance bond/surety for larger projects (links VS-116), workers' compensation/SSS for the installer's crew, and coverage adequacy
Document & gate onboarding: capture verification evidence, gate onboarding (W4989) on verified license+insurance, set re-verification (W5006), and manage exceptions/remediation; feed TPRM (VS-161)

Track & adjust: monitor coverage/fill-rate improvement, adjust targets, and feed network strategy (W4985) and the store-opening plan (VS-37)

Controls: - CTL-746: code-of-conduct enforced; disputes/ethics managed; installers treated fairly; retention tracked

Pain Points / Risks: - **Conduct-breach risk**: Installer misconduct → customer harm/brand damage; mitigated by code & enforcement

- **Fairness risk**: Discriminatory/unfair treatment of installers → grievance/legal; mitigated by fair governance

steps.activity: Establish governance & code-of-conduct: the installer code-of-conduct (workmanship, honesty, customer treatment, no-kickback, no-predatory pricing, RA 10667 competition links VS-129), the ethics/ABC expectations (links VS-119/VS-86), the dispute-resolution framework (W5005), and the governance body

Manage installer relationships: regular communication, an installer council/forum for feedback, training/enablement (links VS-123/VS-124), recognition/top-performer programs, and retention of preferred installers
Enforce & remediate: monitor conduct, enforce the code (warnings/suspension/removal W5005), manage disputes/ethics breaches (VS-119), and ensure fair/non-discriminatory treatment of installers
